name: Lincoln Quirk
current_role: Co-founder and Head of Product, Wave Mobile Money
profile: Co-founded Sendwave (low-fee US/UK-to-Africa remittances, sold to WorldRemit in 2020) and then Wave, a mobile money company that has grown into one of francophone West Africa's largest fintechs, starting in Senegal and valued around $1.7-2B. He met CEO Drew Durbin as a freshman hallmate at Brown and still leads product at Wave.
interesting_fact: Says he and his co-founders build Wave 'primarily for EA reasons'; he attended his first effective altruism gathering in 2013 (about 50 people in an Oakland house) and says he has had more impact through direct work at Wave than through donations.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2020 EA Forum AMA with CTO Ben Kuhn he said he personally wrote much of the original code for both Sendwave and Wave; Sendwave's pitch was sending money by phone number at a 3% fee vs the typical 8-12%.
notes: Low-profile; active in effective altruism circles (EA Forum). Best route likely via Wave or EA community. No published personal email found.

name: Shu Congxuan
current_role: Founder of Laoxiangji (Home Original Chicken), Hefei, Anhui (chairman in 2020; current formal title not confirmed)
profile: Former soldier who began raising chickens in Feixi, Anhui in 1982 and became one of the province's largest free-range chicken farmers. After a 1999 franchising course he opened the 'Feixi Old Hen' fast-food restaurant in Hefei in 2003, renamed Laoxiangji in 2012. The chain now has about 1,400 stores and has repeatedly attempted an IPO; his children hold most of the stake.
interesting_fact: In February 2020 he posted a video tearing up a letter in which employees offered to work without pay during COVID, saying he would sell houses and cars to keep about 16,000 staff fed and employed; it went viral and earned him the nickname 'China's best boss'.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving the army at 20 in autumn 1982, he spent his 1,800-yuan wedding money on about 1,000 chickens and reportedly ate and slept in the chicken shed for seven years while learning the trade.
notes: Chinese-language media only; reach via Laoxiangji corporate (Hefei). Reported to have transferred his direct shareholding to his children; daughter Shu Wen is an executive director.

name: Evan Doll
current_role: Rejoined Apple in 2016 as Director of Health Software Engineering (current role not confirmed by recent sources)
profile: Stanford 2003 grad who joined Apple as an engineer and worked on the original iPhone software (2003-2009). In 2010 he co-founded Flipboard, the magazine-style news app, with Mike McCue and led engineering/product; he left in 2015 for an EIR stint at Redpoint Ventures and returned to Apple in 2016 to direct health software engineering.
interesting_fact: Helped build the original iPhone's software as a senior iPhone engineer at Apple before leaving to co-found Flipboard, one of the breakout iPad apps of 2010.
deep_cut_fact: Grew up in Healdsburg, California (Healdsburg High class of 1999, senior class president). While at Apple he taught an iPhone app programming class on the side and persuaded management to let him keep teaching: 'Teaching is a way to gain mastery.'
notes: Low public profile since returning to Apple; no recent interviews or published contacts. Apple employees rarely do outside media without Apple PR approval.

name: Avi Shua
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Innovation Officer and board member, Orca Security
profile: Israeli cybersecurity veteran (Unit 8200/IDF, then a decade-plus at Check Point, rising to Chief Technologist for threat prevention). Co-founded Orca Security in 2019 and was CEO until March 2023, building its agentless 'SideScanning' cloud security platform to a ~$1.8B valuation; he now leads innovation (SideScanning, Unified Data Model) as CIO.
interesting_fact: Orca's core idea, 'SideScanning', reads cloud workloads' block storage via the cloud provider's APIs instead of installing agents, giving full-stack visibility without touching running workloads.
deep_cut_fact: On CyberWire's 'Career Notes' he said he has been excited about cybersecurity since age 13, when he started probing his high school's network, and advised 'try to do things by yourself'.
notes: info@orca.security is Orca's general company email, not personal. Frequent conference speaker/podcast guest on cloud security, so a podcast invite fits his pattern.

name: Suhail Doshi
current_role: Founder and CEO, Playground (AI graphic design/image model company)
profile: Self-taught programmer who left Arizona State to co-found product-analytics company Mixpanel with Tim Trefren (YC Summer 2009), serving as CEO until 2018. He then built Mighty (a browser streamed from a data center) before pivoting to Playground, an AI-first graphics editor that trains its own image models.
interesting_fact: Mixpanel's idea came from his 2008 internship at Max Levchin's Slide, where he saw the company spending over $1M to build its own internal analytics, as Zynga and others were doing too.
deep_cut_fact: He landed the Slide internship via an offer over IRC while a computer systems engineering student at ASU; Levchin tried to hire him full-time after three months, but he went back to school and then left to start Mixpanel.
notes: Very active on X (@Suhail) and a frequent podcast guest (Latent Space, YC Lightcone) - X is the most natural public route. Data-center angle: Mighty streamed Chrome from cloud servers; Playground trains large diffusion models.

name: Komsan Lee
current_role: Founder and CEO, Flash Group (Flash Express), Thailand
profile: Thai entrepreneur (also spelled Komsan Saelee) who launched parcel-delivery firm Flash Express in 2017-18 with a 25-baht starting fee that undercut rivals charging 60 baht. Flash Group, now spanning logistics, fulfillment, payments and tech, became Thailand's first unicorn in 2021 after a $150M Series D+/E led by SCB 10X and Buer Capital; he still leads it with co-founder/COO Weijie Di.
interesting_fact: On becoming Thailand's first unicorn founder at 29, he said: 'Regardless of how poor you are, which surname you have or where you graduated from, you can become a unicorn startup if you select the right industry... and have a good team.'
deep_cut_fact: Born to a poor family of Chinese descent in Doi Wawee, Chiang Rai, he ran his first business, a local grocery shop, in his first year of university, then worked as a property sales agent and freight forwarder and ran a logistics firm shipping to the US, Japan and China before Flash.
notes: Bangkok Post named him 2021 Start-up Founder of the Year. Interviews are mostly with Thai media (Bangkok Post, The Story Thailand). Flash has pushed EV delivery motorbikes with battery swapping at PTT stations, a possible energy angle.

name: Nathaniel Fernhoff
current_role: Co-founder and CEO (since May 2025), Orca Bio
profile: Scientist-founder (Stanford BS in biology and math, UC Berkeley PhD) who co-founded Menlo Park cell-therapy company Orca Bio in 2016 with Ivan Dimov and Jeroen Bekaert, serving as CSO before becoming CEO in 2025. Orca builds high-precision donor-cell therapies for blood cancers; its lead product Orca-T won FDA approval as Tregzi on June 30, 2026.
interesting_fact: Tregzi (Orca-T), approved by the FDA in June 2026, is described as the first approved therapy built on highly purified regulatory T cells, aimed at improving chronic-GVHD-free survival after matched-donor stem cell transplants.
deep_cut_fact: Before Orca he was an NIH Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA postdoctoral scholar in Irving Weissman's stem-cell lab at Stanford, and he holds two Stanford bachelor's degrees, in biological sciences and in mathematics.
notes: Goes by Nate Fernhoff. Biotech rather than energy/data-center fit; timely hook is the 2026 Tregzi approval and commercial launch. Route via Orca Bio corporate communications.

name: Runik Mehrotra
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, Vise (per April 2025 release; also described as co-head/CIO)
profile: Detroit-area math prodigy who co-founded Vise, an AI-driven portfolio management platform for financial advisors, with Samir Vasavada; the pair raised from Sequoia, Founders Fund and Ribbit while still teenagers and reached a ~$1B valuation. He oversees the AI models behind portfolio construction; Vise passed $15B in platform assets in 2025.
interesting_fact: He and Vasavada met at 13 at a Northwestern University summer research program; before Vise they ran an AI consultancy that was paid $700 an hour to teach finance 'experts' about AI.
deep_cut_fact: Explaining his edge, he told TechCrunch: 'what underlies AI is math'. He also called asset management 'an unsexy industry that makes all of the money in finance.'
notes: Co-founder Samir Vasavada is the more public face of Vise. No published press email found. Mehrotra's title has varied (CTO in 2019, later CIO, Co-CEO in 2025).

name: Trivikraman Thampy
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Games24x7 (Mumbai)
profile: IIT Bombay engineer with an NYU economics PhD who co-founded Games24x7 in 2006 with fellow NYU alumnus Bhavin Pandya. The company built RummyCircle and fantasy-sports app My11Circle into one of India's largest online skill-gaming businesses, backed by Tiger Global and Malabar; it also runs an investment arm, Games24x7 Ventures.
interesting_fact: He says Games24x7 turned profitable within 18 months of starting operations, and that RummyCircle was profitable by 2012 even though it took years to convince investors that skill gaming differed from gambling.
deep_cut_fact: Goes by 'Vikram'. He founded Games24x7 on a 'science of gaming' ethos, applying the behavioral economics from his NYU economics PhD (completed 2008) to model player behavior and personalize gameplay.
notes: Formerly styled Co-CEO alongside Bhavin Pandya; recent releases call him co-founder & CEO. Real-money gaming in India faced heavy regulatory change in 2025, so check the business's current state before outreach. No published press email found.

name: Jinglan Wang
current_role: Co-founder of Optimism; CEO of OP Labs (previously CEO/Executive Director of the Optimism Foundation)
profile: Known as Jing Wang, she co-founded the nonprofit scaling-research group Plasma Group with Karl Floersch, which evolved into Optimism, the Ethereum Layer 2 whose open-source OP Stack underpins Coinbase's Base and many other 'Superchain' networks. She was CEO of Optimism PBC, led the Optimism Foundation after the 2022 split, and has since been reported as CEO of OP Labs.
interesting_fact: The OP Stack she helped build became one of the most widely adopted rollup frameworks; co-founder Ben Jones said 'if you have to put the finger on the pulse of the lifeline of the Optimism Collective, it is Jing Wang.'
deep_cut_fact: She came to crypto via Bitcoin; Vitalik Buterin nudged her toward Ethereum and introduced her to Karl Floersch, who mentored her and gave her a 'textbook' writing project on Plasma, the pre-rollup scaling design that led to Plasma Group and then Optimism (per her July 2023 a16z crypto startup school talk).
notes: Publicly goes by Jing Wang. Active in crypto media (a16z, Epicenter podcast). Exact current title has shifted between Foundation and OP Labs; confirm before outreach.

name: Bo Marr
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, CHAOS Industries (since 2022); co-founder and former CTO of Epirus
profile: Electrical engineer (Duke BS; Georgia Tech MS/PhD; NSF Fellow) who began at IBM and spent about a decade at Raytheon on RF and electronic-warfare systems. He co-founded Epirus in 2018 and served as CTO (briefly interim CEO in 2020) as it developed its Leonidas high-power-microwave counter-drone system, then co-founded radar/defense-tech startup CHAOS Industries in 2022.
interesting_fact: At Raytheon he won the CEO award for innovation, filed more than 70 US and international patents, was a technical lead on the Next Generation Jammer program, and as elected IP Champion reviewed some 600 inventions.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career at IBM, where he co-engineered the chips behind Watson, the system that won Jeopardy! in 2011.
notes: Now focused on CHAOS Industries; some reports style him co-CEO there (unverified). Epirus's contact form is for his former company. Strong energy/power-electronics angle (GaN high-power microwave). Web-search budget ran out during this profile, so CHAOS details are from profile sites only.

name: Nitin Agarwal
current_role: Co-founder of GlobalBees (company now led by Anuj Jain; his current role not confirmed)
profile: Co-founded GlobalBees, an Indian e-commerce brand roll-up that acquires and scales D2C brands, in 2021 with FirstCry founder Supam Maheshwari. GlobalBees became a unicorn in December 2021, one of India's fastest to do so, after buying brands such as The Better Home, andMe, Yellow Chimes and Reach. The company's site now says it is led by Anuj Jain.
interesting_fact: GlobalBees reached unicorn status in December 2021, its founding year, one of the fastest Indian startups to do so.
notes: Very common name; identity tied to GlobalBees only. The web-search budget ran out before his current role or a deep-cut fact could be verified (he appears no longer to run GlobalBees). contact@globalbees.com is a general company inbox.

name: Jake Adams
current_role: Listed as a founder of Genies (role not verified)
profile: Listed as a founder of Genies, the Los Angeles AI-avatar company (founded 2017, valued over $1B, backed by Silver Lake, Breyer Capital, Bond and Bob Iger). Public sources credit CEO Akash Nigam as founder, building Genies partly from the technology of his earlier college app Blend with an unnamed partner; I could not confirm Jake Adams's role.
interesting_fact: Genies has raised about $250M, with investors including Bob Iger, and has partnered with MLB Players Inc., the NBPA, Unity, WEBTOON and Sanrio on AI avatars.
notes: Identity unverified: Wikipedia names only Akash Nigam as founder. 'Jake Adams' is a common name. The web-search budget ran out before his role could be checked, so verify (e.g. LinkedIn, Genies team page) before any outreach.

name: Iddo Gino
current_role: Founder of RapidAPI (now Nokia-owned); per his own site, working on new ideas and advising dev-tools/API companies
profile: Israeli-born, Bay Area-based founder who started RapidAPI as a teenager and spent about a decade building it into what he calls the world's largest API marketplace, used by over 5 million developers and valued at about $1B. RapidAPI is now part of Nokia; he says he is working on new ideas and advising dev-tools and API companies.
interesting_fact: He is a 2017 Thiel Fellow (Peter Thiel's program that pays young people to skip or leave college to build companies) and a Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree.
deep_cut_fact: He keeps a personal Posthaven blog ('Random thoughts') with hands-on tinkering posts, e.g. a Mac Finder automation to right-click any file and copy it as Markdown for AI prompts with Microsoft's markitdown, and fixing Cloudflare 'too many redirects' on Posthaven.
notes: He published the email himself as 'iddo [at] gino.email' on his About page, which makes it the best direct route. Nokia ownership is inferred from Nokia's DPO address on RapidAPI's site; the web-search budget ran out before deal terms could be confirmed.

name: Gina Bartasi
current_role: Founder of Kindbody (fertility clinics); no longer CEO there, current role not verified
profile: Serial fertility-care entrepreneur. Wikipedia lists her as founder of Progyny, the fertility-benefits company (since NASDAQ-listed). She later founded Kindbody, a US chain of fertility and women's-health clinics sold through employers, which reached a roughly $2B valuation; she has since stepped back from the CEO role.
interesting_fact: She has founded two companies in fertility care: Progyny (benefits management) and Kindbody (clinics).
notes: The web-search budget ran out before her current role, a deep-cut fact or a published press contact could be verified. The ginabartasi.com domain is an empty GoDaddy placeholder, not confirmed as hers. Kindbody's leadership and current status should be checked before outreach.

profile: Listed as founder of Harmay, a Chinese cosmetics retailer known for warehouse-style beauty stores, valued at about $1B. I could not verify the biographical details.

name: Gibran El Farizy
current_role: Former co-founder and CEO of eFishery (left after a late-2024 audit)
profile: Gibran Huzaifah (Amsi El Farizy) founded eFishery in Bandung in 2013. The company built automated, IoT-based fish and shrimp feeders and an aquaculture supply/financing platform, and became Indonesia's first aquaculture unicorn. He left the company after a late-2024 audit.
interesting_fact: eFishery's core product was a smart feeder that automates feeding in fish ponds, which grew into a platform serving Indonesian aquaculture farmers.
notes: CAUTION: he left eFishery after a late-2024 audit alleged financial misstatement dating back to 2018. The company reported him to Indonesian police and an investigation was reported as ongoing (allegations, per Wikipedia). Not a suitable outreach target without legal/editorial review. No deep-cut fact recorded, per the positive/neutral rule.

name: Rich Whitney
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Radiology Partners; venture partner/advisor, New Enterprise Associates
profile: Healthcare executive and investor (Penn State BBA, Harvard MBA) who was CFO of dialysis giant DaVita, where he helped lead a turnaround and the acquisitions of Gambro Healthcare and HealthCare Partners. He co-founded Radiology Partners, now the largest US radiology practice, and serves as its chairman and CEO; he is also a venture partner at NEA.
interesting_fact: Radiology Partners credits him with helping lead a DaVita turnaround that created more than $3B in equity value in three years, and with leading the HealthCare Partners deal (now part of Optum).
deep_cut_fact: Besides running Radiology Partners he sits on the boards of, and invests in, CHG Healthcare, Strive Health, US Heart & Vascular and National Veterinary Associates, a veterinary-clinic group.
notes: Radiology Partners publishes no media email; use the contact form. Low personal media profile. AI-in-radiology is a possible podcast angle (unverified here).

name: Hosam Arab
current_role: CEO and Co-founder, Tabby (Riyadh)
profile: Co-founded Tabby, the Middle East's leading buy-now-pay-later and consumer-finance app, now headquartered in Riyadh and serving Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Kuwait. Profitable since 2023, Tabby processes more than $18B in annualised volume for 25M users. In September 2026 it raised $233M at a $6.5B valuation (led by Blue Pool Capital) to expand into credit, wallets (Tabby Cash) and SME finance.
interesting_fact: On the 2026 round he said: 'We began with a button at an online checkout to help people spread costs over time... people deserve more from their money.' Tabby has run employee share tenders since 2023, enabling more than $100M in share sales.
notes: Data-center angle: in Oct 2025 Tabby deployed NVIDIA HGX systems as local 'AI factory' infrastructure in Saudi Arabia for sovereign AI in financial services (https://tabby.ai/en-AE/newsroom/nvidia). The newsroom offers press interviews via press@tabby.ai. The web-search budget ran out before a personal deep-cut fact could be sourced.

name: Stefan Kukman
current_role: CEO, CargoX (Ljubljana, Slovenia)
profile: Slovenian founder and CEO (Štefan Kukman) of CargoX, founded in 2018, which runs a blockchain-based platform for transferring trade documents such as electronic bills of lading. CargoX is the authorised blockchain document-transfer gateway for Egypt's NAFEZA single window (Advance Cargo Information), and in 2025 it went live with the UAE's MPCI programme; it also serves carriers such as Evergreen and HMM.
interesting_fact: CargoX's platform was approved by the International Group of P&I Clubs in February 2020, and it underpins Egypt's national Advance Cargo Information system for import documents.
deep_cut_fact: CargoX demoed its 'Smart B/L' on the public Ethereum blockchain at the International Logistics Congress in Portorož in April 2018, then issued its first commercial one in July 2018 for a shipment from Shanghai to the Slovenian port of Koper.
notes: Spelled Štefan Kukman on the company site. info@cargox.io is the general company email; CargoX also has a press kit (https://cargox.io/press-kit). The web-search budget ran out before personal background could be checked.
